setting_and_country.value: Thèsez-vous structured writing retreats in rural and suburban Quebec, Canada; doctoral researchers mainly in the social sciences
setting_and_country.quote: these retreats occur in various rural and suburban settings throughout the province of Quebec

design.value: Randomised experiment with a waitlist control (explanatory sequential mixed methods), preregistered
design.quote: One hundred doctoral researchers were randomly assigned to either the experimental group (n = 50) or the waitlist control trial group (n = 50).

participants.value: 100 doctoral researchers (76% women); 98 attended a retreat
participants.quote: all participants who experienced a writing retreat (n = 98) were included in the exploratory and qualitative data analyses

group_format.value: Three-day residential structured writing retreat with two facilitators: Pomodoro writing blocks (50 min silent writing, 10 min break), SMART goals and a shared Kanban board
group_format.quote: breaks down work into 50 min intervals of silent writing followed by a 10 min break

comparison.value: Waitlist control (no retreat during the two-week study period)
comparison.quote: Participants in the waitlist control group received the intervention two weeks after their post-test.

confidence_self_efficacy.value: NR (writing confidence or self-efficacy was not measured)

other_writing_outcomes.value: Mental health improved vs. control: psychological distress d = 1.57, emotional wellbeing d = 1.84, psychological wellbeing d = 1.55, social wellbeing d = 0.71; perceived productivity predicted lower distress (β = −0.29) and better wellbeing
other_writing_outcomes.quote: the effects on psychological distress (d  =  1.57) and emotional (d  =  1.84) and psychological (d = 1.55) wellbeing were notably larger

notes: The only randomised comparison with not taking part; outcomes are mental health, with productivity as a perceived aspect of the retreat. Volunteers, so possible selection bias (authors' limitation).
